Coordinate Truck Parking and Container Depot Access

Thematic Area: Depot Operations & Yard Visibility

How might we coordinate truck parking and container gate-in and gate-out movements to improve visibility and operating flow at a container depot?

Background

A shipping and logistics group wants better coordination of truck parking and container entry and exit at its Cibitung depot.

The objective is to establish a clear view of arrivals, parking availability and gate movements so staff can organise depot activity. Relevant partners bring site-mapping, movement tracking, access-management and simulation capabilities.

The collaboration will connect parking and gate workflows around the depot’s layout, operating rules and data sources.

Significance of Problem

Key challenges include:

  • Difficult arrival planning: Truck arrivals must be coordinated with available parking and gate capacity.
  • Slower congestion response: Limited movement visibility makes queues and bottlenecks harder to identify and address.
  • Incomplete visit records: Disconnected parking and gate information complicates tracking of truck and container movements.

Existing Efforts

  • Company priority: Truck parking and container gate-in and gate-out are identified needs at the Cibitung depot.
  • Available capabilities: Compound-mapping and movement/access tools support site assessment and workflow design. University digital-twin research offers simulation of arrival patterns, queues, parking allocation and gate rules.
  • Collaboration focus: Capture current operating data and build a connected parking-and-gate workflow. Define vehicle and container identifiers, linked movement records and operating responsibilities. Use simulation to compare planning options and connect live gate control through the operational system.

Potential Market Size

  • Global yard-management-system market: Global revenue is projected to grow from US$980 million in 2026 to US$4.9 billion by 2032, representing 30.5% annual growth. Gate automation and operational visibility are key adoption drivers across logistics yards.

Eligibility / Qualification

  • Technology readiness: Minimum technology readiness level 3 (TRL3).
  • NUS linkage: NUS student or graduate founder, or incubation through an NUS programme such as BLOCK71.
  • Local and overseas startups: Open to Indonesian and overseas startups.
  • Commitment: Complete the selection process and travel to Indonesia if selected.
